tests.title: Test automations can't make approvals or change permissions; they only send notifications and create tasks
tests.evidence: Spec, Test Tool: 'They can also automate approvals, permissions, and actions off of test results, or lack of taking a test by the deadline.' The full list of actions is `AUTOMATION_ACTIONS = ["NOTIFY_TAKER", "NOTIFY_ADVISOR", "NOTIFY_ADMINS", "CREATE_ADMIN_TASK"]` (types.ts:13). runAutomations (lib/domain/tests.ts:1003-1050) only calls notify() and createTask(). The PASSED task even says a person must do the approval: 'Take whatever step comes next for them (for example, approving a role or access).' Test results only affect permissions through admin-only RoleRequirement (requirements.ts:260 assertRequirementAdmin, which accepts university tests only). So a club test cannot trigger an approval or a permission change, and no test can approve anything automatically.
tests.fix: Add an `APPROVE_JOIN_REQUEST` action (PASSED only) to AUTOMATION_ACTIONS in lib/tests/types.ts and handle it in runAutomations. For club tests, find the taker's PENDING membership in test.clubId and approve it through an actor-less internal helper split out of memberships.decideMembership. decideMembership itself can't be used because it asserts the roster capability on an actor. Run the helper's status update, subscribeInternal, resolveTasks('membership'), logActivity with actorId null and notify. For permissions, add `RESUME_PERMISSIONS` / `PAUSE_PERMISSIONS` actions that call roles.setRolePermissions on the taker's open OFFICER/AMBASSADOR assignment in test.clubId. Add labels for the new actions to actionLabel and list them in AutomationsCard (components/tests/TestBuilder.tsx:626).

tests.title: Officers placed by an election get the seat's default permissions without the setup prompt
tests.evidence: Spec, Permissions: officer permissions are modular and 'the setup is prompted when an officer is promoted'. OFFICER and AMBASSADOR seats can be elected (`ELECTABLE_ROLES = ["PRESIDENT", "VP", "OFFICER", "AMBASSADOR"]`, elections.ts:31). applyElectionResult accepts only `ApplyInput = z.object({ winnerCandidateId: ... })` (line 415) and calls `assignRole(actor, { clubId, userId: winner.userId, positionId, replaceAssignmentIds })` with no permissions (line 458). assignRole then falls back to `v.permissions ?? position.defaultPermissions` (roles.ts:164). ApplyResultPanel (manage/elections/_components/ElectionControls.tsx:154-205) only shows a confirm dialog. It has none of the 'permissions' step that org-chart/_components/AssignDialog.tsx:28 shows for customizable seats.
tests.fix: Add `permissions: z.array(z.string()).optional()` to ApplyInput (elections.ts:415) and pass `permissions: v.permissions` into the assignRole call at line 458. In ApplyResultPanel, when the seat's role is OFFICER or AMBASSADOR, show PermissionChecklist pre-filled with the seat's defaultPermissions before the confirm dialog. Add a permissions argument to applyResult in manage/elections/actions.ts:58.

tests.title: A "Take: <test>" task never closes once its assignment is MISSED and the person uses up their attempts, the test closes or is archived, or the person leaves the audience
tests.evidence: markMissedAssignments sets status MISSED but deliberately leaves the REQUIREMENT task open while the test is still takeable (tests.ts:1083-1087). Every later path that should close it only selects status ASSIGNED: the attempts-exhausted branch `findMany({ where: { ..., cycleKey: attempt.cycleKey, status: "ASSIGNED" } })` (tests.ts:940), archiveTest `findMany({ where: { testId, status: "ASSIGNED" } })` (tests.ts:495), switching the audience to OPEN (tests.ts:169), and `extras = existing.filter((a) => a.status === "ASSIGNED" && ...)` (tests.ts:186). A ONE_OFF test's cycle key is always "once", so the stale-round cleanup (tests.ts:163-164) never fires. When closesAt passes, syncAssignments returns at `if (!isOpenForTaking(test, now)) return` (tests.ts:180) without closing anything. REQUIREMENT is in SELF_CLOSING_KINDS (tasks.ts:44), and setTaskDone refuses to close those by hand (tasks.ts:190-191). Example: the seeded Event Safety Quiz (ONE_OFF, maxAttempts 3, dueDays 30, closesAt set). A member who misses the due date and then fails 3 late attempts sees 'You've used all 3 attempts' (tests.ts:641), but 'Take: Event Safety Quiz' stays in their inbox permanently.
tests.fix: Close the testAssignment task for MISSED rows wherever ASSIGNED rows are released. In applyOutcome's attempts-exhausted branch use `status: { in: ["ASSIGNED", "MISSED"] }` and resolve the tasks; leave MISSED rows MISSED. In archiveTest and both syncAssignments release branches (tests.ts:169, 186), also run `db.task.updateMany({ where: { sourceType: "testAssignment", sourceId: { in: <MISSED ids> }, status: "OPEN" }, data: { status: "CANCELLED", completedAt: now } })`. Before the `!isOpenForTaking` early return (tests.ts:180), cancel open tasks of the current cycle's MISSED assignments.

tests.title: A training requirement can end up pointing at a deleted event and be switched back on, which pauses every leader it applies to
tests.evidence: deleteEvent blocks deletion only when an ACTIVE requirement uses the event: `db.roleRequirement.findFirst({ where: { trainingEventId: eventId, active: true } })` (events.ts:869). The FK is `RoleRequirement_trainingEventId_fkey ... ON DELETE SET NULL` (psql pg_constraint), so deleting the event while the requirement is off nulls trainingEventId. setRequirementActive validates only TEST requirements: `if (active && prev.kind === "TEST" && prev.testId)` (requirements.ts:305-308). A TRAINING requirement with no event can therefore be turned back on, while saveRequirement would reject the same state (requirements.ts:269-271). requirementStatus then never marks it met (`else if (r.kind === "TRAINING" && r.trainingEventId)`, authz/requirements.ts:51), so once graceDays pass `suspended = status.overdue` (authz/index.ts:163) strips every holder's capabilities, and nobody can meet the requirement. By contrast, deleteTest blocks on any requirement, active or not (tests.ts:548).
tests.fix: In deleteEvent, drop `active: true` from the requirement lookup (events.ts:869) so any requirement blocks deletion, as deleteTest does. In setRequirementActive, when `active && prev.kind === "TRAINING"`, load the event and throw invalid(...) unless `prev.trainingEventId` is set, the event exists, and its status is "SCHEDULED".

ai.title: AI assistant can't see or edit the user's account or profile, and has no admin build tools
ai.evidence: Spec, AI Integration: 'help students and administrators build their portions of the platform ... helps users set up their accounts and makes actions on the user's behalf.' TOOLS = [...READ_TOOLS, ...WRITE_TOOLS] (lib/ai/tools.ts:21). The write tools are join_club, subscribe_calendar, unsubscribe_calendar, add_personal_task, add_event_idea, create_event, start_club_draft, invite_advisor, assign_role and post_announcement. None reads or writes the person's own profile: my_clubs_and_roles (read-tools.ts:262-313) returns only platform role, clubs and subscriptions. None builds a university-level item (policy, test, training, requirement). lib/domain/profiles.ts already exports updateProfile/addExperience, and policies.ts exports savePolicy. The assistant's only fallback is the knowledge.ts:24 instruction 'say where in Wildcat Clubs to do it and link the page'.
ai.fix: Following the existing readTool/writeTool pattern: (1) add a `my_profile` read tool that returns the actor's headline, about, majors/minors, classYear, linkedinUrl and which fields are empty; (2) add an `update_my_profile` write tool. Its prepare() loads the current profile, merges in only the fields given (updateProfile replaces every field), shows the changes on the card, and execute() calls profiles.updateProfile(actor, merged); (3) add an admin-gated `draft_policy` write tool that calls policies.savePolicy(actor, null, {..., status: 'DRAFT'}), with an isAdmin(actor) check in prepare(). Register these in READ_TOOLS/WRITE_TOOLS and describe them in lib/ai/knowledge.ts.

ai.title: Assistant's find_club_member is gated on isLeader, not the roster capability, so it shows join month and account kind to leaders without Roster access
ai.evidence: read-tools.ts:744 checks only `if (!access?.isLeader) throw ...` and then returns matching active members with `account` (student or faculty/staff), `joined` (month) and current roles. isLeader is `viaPlatform !== null || rank >= 1` (authz/index.ts:193), which includes an Ambassador with no capabilities and a suspended officer. The roster page requires the `roster` capability (manage/members/page.tsx:18 `loadClubWorkspace(slug, "roster")`). The impact is smaller than reported: in an approved club, every active member can already see names and role labels in the club chat participants sheet (messaging.ts:558-576; canRead at :290). The extra data is join month and account kind, plus names in draft clubs.
ai.fix: In find_club_member, replace the check with `if (!access || !(access.capabilities.has("roster") || access.assignableRoles.length > 0)) throw new ToolError(...)`. That matches the roster page and the assign_role use case.

ai.title: Assistant usage limit resets when conversations are deleted, and the confirm route never checks it
ai.evidence: modelCallsSince counts `db.aiMessage.count({ where: { role: "assistant", createdAt: { gte: since }, conversation: { userId } } })`. AiMessage cascades on conversation delete (prisma/schema.prisma:1472 `onDelete: Cascade`), and deleteConversation hard-deletes (conversations.ts:197 `db.aiConversation.deleteMany`). A DELETE /api/assistant/conversations/<id> therefore erases that conversation's count. app/api/assistant/confirm/route.ts calls `runTurn({ ..., mode: { kind: "continue" } })` without checking HOURLY_LIMIT; only app/api/assistant/route.ts:37 checks it.
ai.fix: Count usage in rows that deleting a conversation doesn't touch: add an AiUsage table (userId, createdAt) written once per model call in runTurn, and have modelCallsSince count it. Or make deleteConversation a soft delete. Export HOURLY_LIMIT and run the same 429 check in confirm/route.ts before calling runTurn.

ai.title: Assistant's create_event card says a Meet link will be added once sync is on, but the request isn't saved
ai.evidence: write-tools.ts:307 `where = link ? `Online (${link})` : "Online — a Google Meet link is added when Google Calendar sync is on"`. createMeetLink is used only during this one save (events.ts:662 `mirror(event.id, actor, f.createMeetLink)`) and is never stored. fieldsFromEvent sets `createMeetLink: false` (events.ts:715), and normalizeLocation stores `virtualUrl: l.virtualUrl || null`. If sync is off or the club has no contactEmail, the event is saved as online with no join link, and nothing adds one later. The Events Builder's copy is correct (LocationFields.tsx:147 'created once a system administrator turns it on and you save the event again').
ai.fix: In create_event's prepare, call `googleCalendarReady(club.id)`. If it isn't live and google_meet is requested with no link, either throw a ToolError ('Google Calendar sync is off, so a Meet link can't be made. Paste a join link instead.') or change the card line to 'Online. No join link yet: Google Calendar sync is off, so add a link in the Events Builder before the event.'

ai.title: Assistant markdown link filter treats `/\host` as an internal path
ai.evidence: `if (/^\/(?!\/)[^\s]*$/.test(href)) return href;` accepts `/\evil.example/login`. The href is taken raw from `src.slice(close + 2, paren)` (markdown.ts:107). isExternalHref only checks `startsWith("/")`, so Markdown.tsx renders it as a same-tab next/link `<Link>` with no 'opens in a new tab' note. The app-dir link (next/dist/client/app-dir/link.js) doesn't normalize backslashes; only the pages-router resolve-href.js does. Browsers resolve `/\evil.example` to https://evil.example. The function's own comment promises 'never //host'.
ai.fix: Change the first test in safeHref to `/^\/(?![\/\\])[^\s\\]*$/`, which rejects a backslash anywhere in a site path, so these links render as plain text.

roles.title: Seed has only 3 role contributions (projects/files on roles), all for 2 hand-written personas
roles.evidence: Spec: 'Please populate a flush mock database for user testing' and 'you'll see their contributions to the club and the actual projects and files ... attached to the roles they took.' The /clubs/[slug]/history page lists contributions from Project rows (history/page.tsx:199-224). The seed's proj() helper (files.ts:282-285) is called only 3 times (lines 286, 287, 296). DB: Project has 3 rows (applied-ai-lab ×2, wildcat-robotics ×1) and ProjectFile has 4 rows, against 911 RoleAssignment rows (632 ended) and 79 alumni. The history page of every other club shows no contributions.
roles.fix: In prisma/seed/steps/files.ts, after line 296, go through each seeded approved or retired club's ended PRESIDENT/VP/OFFICER assignments (ctx.club(...).assignments). roles.title: When WSUSA rejects a club, a pending advisor invite leaves the invitee with an inbox task they can never close
roles.evidence: decideClub with REJECT changes status and resolves only the "club" and "departmentRequest" tasks (clubs.ts:549-554). PENDING AdvisorInvite rows and their USER APPROVAL tasks stay open. Invites can still be sent while a club is SUBMITTED (inviteAdvisor blocks only REJECTED, advisors.ts:92), so a second invite can be pending at review time. Both accept and decline go through loadInviteForAnswer, which throws `if (invite.club.status === "RETIRED" || invite.club.status === "REJECTED") throw conflict("This club is no longer active, so the invitation has closed.")` (advisors.ts:155) before anything is written. loadInviteForViewer still returns `canAnswer: true` for a PENDING invite (advisors.ts:145). APPROVAL is in SELF_CLOSING_KINDS, so setTaskDone refuses it (tasks.ts:190-191). On the club side, the settings page passes `canInvite={access.canInviteAdvisor && live}`, where live is false for REJECTED clubs (settings/page.tsx:25, 71), so founders aren't prompted to clean up either. retireClub does cancel invites (clubs.ts:632), but rejection doesn't.
roles.fix: In decideClub, when v.decision === "REJECT", inside the existing transaction: find the club's PENDING advisor invites, `tx.advisorInvite.updateMany({ where: { clubId: club.id, status: "PENDING" }, data: { status: "CANCELLED", respondedAt: now } })`, and call `resolveTasks("advisorInvite", invite.id, actor.id, tx, "CANCELLED")` for each one.

roles.title: Seeded test assignments have no inbox tasks, and nothing backfills them
roles.evidence: The seed writes TestAssignment rows directly: `ctx.rows.testAssignments.push({ ..., testId: quizId, ..., status, ... })` (governance.ts:350), with no matching task row. Officer requirements get explicit tasks (governance.ts:277-290); the quiz gets none. psql: the 'Event Safety Quiz' (CLUB_MEMBERS, ONE_OFF, cycle 'once') has 54 ASSIGNED rows, and Task has no rows with sourceType 'testAssignment'. syncAssignments creates tasks only for `fresh = [...missing, ...returning]` (tests.ts:200-216), so these existing ASSIGNED rows never get one, and the 54 members never see the quiz in /tasks. The 5 NEEDS_REVIEW attempts (seeded at governance.ts:100) also have no 'testAttempt' grading task. submitAbandonedAttempts would backfill those (tests.ts:1112-1125), but the testAssignment tasks have no backfill anywhere. Rated low because the production write path creates the tasks; the gap shows up in the seeded/demo data and in any assignment whose task insert failed.
roles.fix: In governance.ts, push a matching REQUIREMENT task (`sourceType: "testAssignment", sourceId: <assignment id>, assigneeType: "USER", title: "Take: Event Safety Quiz", href: /tests/<id>, dueAt`) for each ASSIGNED quiz row, and a 'testAttempt' grading task for each NEEDS_REVIEW attempt. Optionally, in syncAssignments, also create the missing task for ASSIGNED rows of the current cycle that have no OPEN testAssignment task.

roles.title: In role history, alumni can still edit their retired profile, and org-chart editors can permanently delete projects a student wrote on their own profile
roles.evidence: profiles.ts:30-33 assertCanEditProfile blocks ALUMNI ('Your profile was retired when you graduated, so it can't be changed') for addProject, updateProject and deleteProject (the last two also require p.userId === actor.id). roles.ts:520-524 canCurateRole is `if (assignment.userId === actor.id) return true; ... access?.capabilities.has("orgchart")`, with no status check. addRoleContribution (531) creates a Project for the holder, and removeRoleContribution (580-587) runs `await db.project.delete({ where: { id: p.id } })` for the holder or any orgchart holder. The history page sets `curator = isSelf || canCurate` (history/page.tsx:167) and shows ContributionDialog and RemoveContributionButton with no alumni check (194, 216). ALUMNI accounts can sign in, because session.ts:87 rejects only DEACTIVATED. The profile editor writes the same rows when the student links a project to a role (profiles.ts addProject with roleAssignmentId), so an org-chart editor can hard-delete a project the student wrote, files included. DB: gwentorres (ALUMNI) owns 'Advising FAQ Chatbot' and 'Prompt Engineering Workshop Series', both role-linked. Rated medium, not high: contracts.md:97 deliberately lets leaders add contributions for holders.
roles.fix: In roles.ts canCurateRole, let the holder through only when `actor.status === "ACTIVE"` (and hide the dialog and remove button in history/page.tsx:167 when the viewer is ALUMNI). In removeRoleContribution, when actor.id !== p.userId, unlink instead of delete: `db.project.update({ where: { id }, data: { roleAssignmentId: null, clubId: null } })`. Only the owner deletes, through profiles.deleteProject or the holder path.

roles.title: Advisor memberships written by grantRole are still counted as members on several screens, so member counts disagree
roles.evidence: grantRole upserts `source: input.role === "ADVISOR" ? "ADVISOR" : "REGISTER"`, status ACTIVE (roles.ts:69-73). The reviewer's main citation is out of date: the current working tree already limits metrics registeredCounts to `user: { kind: "STUDENT" }` (metrics/index.ts:252, an uncommitted change), and the curl to :3200 hit a build from before that change. The inline counts did not change. ClubDashboard.tsx:37 uses `db.membership.count({ where: { clubId, status: "ACTIVE" } })` for 'Members / Registered members', and the attendance tracker uses the same count at manage/attendance/page.tsx:67 ('of N registered', :102). membershipGrowthFor (analytics/clubs.ts:96) has no kind filter, so admin analytics shows 'X registered members now' (:197) next to the student-only 'Registered members' stat (:169). The attendance-rate denominator `members_at_time` (metrics/index.ts:435) and loadOccurrenceAttendees (attendance/queries.ts:315-328) include advisor memberships too. DB: 44 ACTIVE memberships belong to faculty or staff, and ceramics-guild and astronomy-club each have 8 ACTIVE memberships for 7 students. So the club dashboard shows 8 while the club page shows 7.
roles.fix: Keep advisor memberships, since activeMemberIds uses them for announcements and chat, but count them in one place. Export registeredMemberCount(clubId) from lib/metrics (wrapping registeredCounts) and use it in ClubDashboard.tsx:37 and manage/attendance/page.tsx:67. Add the same student filter (JOIN "User" u ... u.kind = 'STUDENT') to the member numerator and the members_at_time denominator in clubAttendanceByOccurrence and in loadOccurrenceAttendees, and add `user: { kind: "STUDENT" }` to membershipGrowthFor.

roles.title: Several role-ending paths skip reopenRequirementTasks, so officer requirement tasks and test assignments stay open until the next cron tick
roles.evidence: endRoleAssignment calls `await reopenRequirementTasks(a.userId)` (roles.ts:214), whose comment says 'Requirements they no longer owe close right away instead of waiting for the job'. These paths end roles with raw writes and no re-sync: leaveClub (memberships.ts:90), removeMember (:110), handOffPresidency with becomeAlumni (roles.ts:310), endPlacement (roles.ts:447), grantRole's endAssignmentIds used by assignRole replacement and the hand-off (roles.ts:64), and retireClub (clubs.ts:627; it cancels club-tagged tasks but leaves TestAssignments ASSIGNED). syncAllRequirementHolders cleans these up on the 15-minute tick, but it runs after 'Missed test deadlines' (jobs/tick.ts:66-74). If a due date falls in that window, markMissedAssignments (tests.ts:1069-1090) marks someone who has already left as MISSED and runs MISSED_DEADLINE automations.
roles.fix: Call reopenRequirementTasks(userId) after the transaction in leaveClub, removeMember, handOffPresidency (becomeAlumni), endPlacement and retireClub (for each affected user), and in grantRole for the users in endAssignmentIds. In lib/jobs/tick.ts, move the 'Officer requirements' job before 'Missed test deadlines'.

roles.title: The retired-club summary counts 'Events held' differently from lib/metrics (co-hosted events are left out)
roles.evidence: `db.eventOccurrence.count({ where: { event: { clubId: club.id }, status: "SCHEDULED", startsAt: { lte: club.retiredAt ?? new Date() }, attendances: { some: {} } } })` counts hosted occurrences only. lib/metrics/index.ts:36-37 defines a held event as counting 'for the host and every approved co-host' (clubOccurrences UNION with EventCohost). The 'Members over time' count on line 16 also includes advisor memberships. The current retired clubs have no co-hosted held events, so the numbers match today. The other duplicates the reviewer listed (tracker average, loadOccurrenceAttendees, dashboard and /me term counts) give the same results as metrics and are dropped.
roles.fix: Add clubHeldEventCount(clubId, { to }) to lib/metrics, built on clubOccurrences plus HAS_CHECKIN, and call it from RetiredSummary.tsx:17.

roles.title: The advisor-removal rules contradict each other: endRoleAssignment lets any advisor end a co-advisor's role, but removeMember allows only admins
roles.evidence: roles.ts:186-187: `const full = access.viaPlatform !== null || access.isAdvisor; if (a.role === "ADVISOR" && !full) throw forbidden("Only an admin or the advisor can end an advisor's role.")`. Here `full` is true for any advisor of the club, not only the advisor being removed. memberships.ts:106 says 'Only an admin can remove an advisor', and members/page.tsx:37 mirrors that. The org-chart UI doesn't list advisors, so this is reachable only by calling the endRole server action (org-chart/actions.ts:30) directly with another advisor's assignmentId.
roles.fix: In endRoleAssignment, change the advisor check to `if (a.role === "ADVISOR" && !access.viaPlatform && !self) throw forbidden(...)`, so only admins or the advisor themself can end it, matching removeMember.

roles.title: UI copy hard-codes the 'active member' rule instead of reading the sysadmin-editable config
roles.evidence: '"Active" means they attended in the last month or at one of the club's last two events' (MembersTable.tsx:253). Similar fixed text appears in elections/page.tsx:101, ClubAnalyticsTable.tsx:246, members/page.tsx:102 and ClubDashboard.tsx:62 ('Attended in the last month or recent events'). roles.title: Alumni and faculty see 'Leave a review' / 'You can now review', but writeReview always refuses them
roles.evidence: `reviewEligible: attended >= threshold` (metrics/index.ts:540) and `reviewEligibility` → `{ eligible: attended >= required }` (lines 597-602) ignore account kind and status. writeReview refuses `actor.kind !== "STUDENT"` and `actor.status !== "ACTIVE"` (domain/reviews.ts:41-42). The flag reaches the app through toAttendanceSummary (api/m/_lib/serialize.ts:133) and through reviewProgressFor (domain/attendance.ts:107-110). The app then shows `Leave a review` (mobile club/[slug].tsx:321-322) and 'You can now review {club}' (CheckinResultView.tsx:78-86). The web has the same problem (ClubAttendanceRecord.tsx:73 'You can leave a review'). DB check: gwen.torres@mail.weber.edu is kind=STUDENT, status=ALUMNI, with 81 check-ins at Applied AI Lab, and the threshold is 3 (lib/config reviews.minAttendance). She is offered a review link, and submitting the review is refused.
roles.fix: Put the account rule in the metrics layer. In summariesFor (metrics/index.ts:505), add `db.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId }, select: { kind: true, status: true } })` to the Promise.all and compute `canReview = kind === 'STUDENT' && status === 'ACTIVE'`. Set `reviewEligible: canReview && attended >= threshold` and expose `canReview` on MemberClubSummary, MAttendanceSummary and reviewEligibility(). The UIs (mobile AttendanceCard and CheckinResultView, web ClubAttendanceRecord) should render the review row only when `canReview` is true. Otherwise a false flag would show '81 of 3 events toward leaving a review'.

roles.evidence: `{holders.length}/{maxHolders}`. Touch devices never show a title, and screen readers read "1/2" as a fraction.

google.title: Any club leader, including the founder of a draft club, picks which Workspace user the Google service account impersonates (contactEmail)
google.evidence: All three sync adapters impersonate Club.contactEmail through domain-wide delegation: google-drive.ts:119 `await work(await client(club.contactEmail), club, new Ctx(club.id))`, google-calendar.ts:139 `const subject = e.club?.contactEmail ?? PLATFORM_SENDER`, google-chat.ts:72 `const chat = await client(club.contactEmail)`. The only check on the field is its format: clubs.ts:51-58 `optionalEmail` (z.email refine). setClubContactEmail (clubs.ts:346-349) needs only `assertClubCap(actor, v.clubId, "profile")`, and createClub accepts `contactEmail: optionalEmail` (clubs.ts:180, saved at :219). authz/index.ts:64 gives DRAFT clubs `["profile", "orgchart", "constitution", "files"]`. Opening Club Files runs prepareClubFiles → drive.backfillClubDrive (domain/files.ts:607-609). driveReady and schedule only check integrationLive and that contactEmail is set; they do not check club status. backfillClubDrive → rootFolder (google-drive.ts:177-192) creates a folder in the impersonated account's Drive, and shareRootWithLeaders gives the club's leaders writer access. syncPermissions adds `type: "anyone"` reader access to PUBLIC files. So once Drive sync is on, any student can found a draft whose contactEmail is a dean's or another club's @weber.edu address. The student then writes into a folder owned by that account and can publish anyone-with-link files from it. After approval, Chat spaces and messages (google-chat.ts:74-84, 108-113) and calendars (google-calendar.ts:118-120) are also created as that person.
google.fix: Take the delegation subject away from club leaders. Add an admin-only setter, e.g. a new Club.googleAccountEmail set through an authz action under admin.clubs, and have liveClub/driveReady (google-drive.ts), googleCalendarReady/loadEvent (google-calendar.ts) and googleChatReady/ensureClubChatSpace/loadForMirror (google-chat.ts) read that field instead of contactEmail. contactEmail then stays as display-only contact info. If a schema change isn't wanted now, setClubContactEmail and createClub should at least reject an address that equals any User.email (case-insensitive), PLATFORM_SENDER, or another club's contactEmail, and should require it to match a configured club-account allow-list or pattern.

google.title: Email header injection: club names and event titles go into the raw Gmail Subject header without removing CR/LF
google.evidence:
email.ts:24-27 builds the message as `[`From: ...`, `To: ${input.to}`, `Subject: ${input.subject}`, "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8", "", text].join("
")` and sends it raw through gmail.users.messages.send. Subjects include user text: advisors.ts sendInvite `emailAddress(invite.email, `Will you advise ${club.name}?`, ...)`, announcements.ts:155 `New announcement in ${club.name}`, and events.ts tellCohostsAboutChange `“${event.title}” was cancelled` (email: true). The schemas only trim and cap length, so internal 
 passes: clubs.ts:163 `NameInput = z.string(...).trim().min(3).max(100)` and events.ts:94 `title: z.string().trim().min(1).max(140)`. parseForm (clubs.ts:31) does no other cleaning. createClubAction (app/clubs/new/actions.ts:6) passes the client object straight to createClub. A student can therefore found a draft named `X
Bcc: victims@...

<body>` and invite any @weber.edu advisor. Gmail honors the injected Bcc and body, so the platform's official sender delivers mail the attacker wrote. This applies once the email integration is live; psql shows no current club names containing CR/LF. Subjects are also sent without RFC 2047 encoding, even though the platform's subjects routinely contain “ ” and —.
google.fix: In sendEmail (email.ts), normalize the subject before building the message: `const subject = input.subject.replace(/[\r\n\t\u0000-\u001f\u007f]+/g, " ").trim()`. Reject a `to` that contains CR/LF. Encode the Subject as `=?UTF-8?B?${Buffer.from(subject).toString("base64")}?=` and add a `MIME-Version: 1.0` header. As defense in depth, add `.refine((v) => !/[\r\n]/.test(v))` to NameInput (clubs.ts:163), the event title (events.ts:94) and the announcement title schema.

google.title: Changing a club's Google account keeps the old calendar, Drive folder and Chat space IDs, so every later sync fails
google.evidence: setClubContactEmail runs `await db.club.update({ where: { id: v.clubId }, data: { contactEmail: v.contactEmail } })` and changes only the email. The adapters then call the new subject against the old account's resources. google-calendar.ts:117 `if (e.club.googleCalendarId) return e.club.googleCalendarId` → patch and then insert into a calendar the new user can't reach, so the sync fails. google-drive.ts:178 `if (club.googleDriveFolderId) return club.googleDriveFolderId` → files.create with that parent fails. backfill only picks rows with `driveFileId: null` (google-drive.ts:336), so files already copied keep their old-account IDs. google-chat.ts:70 reuses googleChatSpaceId, which the new account isn't in. Grep finds no code that ever sets googleCalendarId, googleDriveFolderId, googleChatSpaceId, FileItem.driveFileId or Event.googleEventId back to null, except a test (files.integration.test.ts:186-187). The only way out is editing the database.
google.fix: In setClubContactEmail, read the current contactEmail. When the normalized new value differs, do the following in one transaction: set googleCalendarId, googleDriveFolderId and googleChatSpaceId to null on the club, run `db.fileItem.updateMany({ where: { clubId }, data: { driveFileId: null } })` and `db.event.updateMany({ where: { clubId }, data: { googleEventId: null } })`, and log it. Conversation.googleSpaceId needs nothing, because ensureClubChatSpace re-points it to the new space (google-chat.ts:86). If the delegation subject moves to an admin-only field (first finding), put this reset in that setter.

google.title: Expo push errors are recorded as SENT, and rejected device tokens are never removed
google.evidence: push.ts:19-25 POSTs a single message to https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send and records `status: res.ok ? "SENT" : "FAILED", error: res.ok ? null : await res.text()`. Expo's push API returns HTTP 200 for per-message errors and puts them in the body (`{ data: { status: "error", message, details: { error: "DeviceNotRegistered" } } }`), so these are logged as SENT with no error. The only pushToken deletion in the codebase is on sign-out (domain/devices.ts:39 `deleteMany({ where: { token, userId: actor.id } })`), so dead tokens keep getting sent to.
google.fix: In sendPush, parse `const j = await res.json().catch(() => null)`. Record FAILED with `error: j?.data?.message ?? (await text)` when `!res.ok || j?.data?.status === "error"`. When `j?.data?.details?.error === "DeviceNotRegistered"`, run `db.pushToken.deleteMany({ where: { token } })`.

google.title: Google Calendar uses the full `auth/calendar` scope under domain-wide delegation, while Drive uses the narrow scope
google.evidence: `const SCOPES = ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar"];`. With domain-wide delegation, the Workspace admin grants scopes per client ID, so this lets the service account read and write every calendar of any impersonated user. The adapter only calls calendars.insert (google-calendar.ts:118) and events on that calendar, plus events on PLATFORM_SENDER's `primary` (line 116). Drive deliberately uses `drive.file` and documents it (google-drive.ts:46, contracts.md:476). The calendar scope is not documented anywhere for the admin's delegation setup.
google.fix: Switch SCOPES to `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.app.created`. For university events, create an app-owned secondary calendar in the platform account the same way calendarIdFor does for clubs, store its ID in SystemConfig, and use it instead of "primary", so no broader scope is needed. Note that delegation grants can't be limited to one subject. Document the scope in the google-calendar.ts header and contracts.md, as Drive does.

google.title: Retiring a club cancels WSUSA's open funding, invoice, document and review tasks, but the records behind them stay pending
google.evidence: retireClub runs `tx.task.updateMany({ where: { clubId: club.id, status: "OPEN" }, data: { status: "CANCELLED", ... } })`. That matches every task tagged with the club, including ADMINS tasks: funding APPROVAL (funding.ts:566-577, `clubId: club.id, source: funding`), INVOICE (funding.ts:711-722, `clubId: request.clubId`), clubDocument (constitution.ts:271-279), departmentRequest (clubs.ts:333-341), and reviewBombing/reviewFlag (reviews.ts:94-101, 145-153). retireClub never changes the records themselves, even though its docstring says "open requests close". A SUBMITTED FundingRequest stays SUBMITTED, an OPEN Invoice stays OPEN, and a PENDING_APPROVAL ClubDocument stays pending. decideFundingRequest (funding.ts:636-655) and decideCustomDocument (constitution.ts:313-318) don't check club status, so WSUSA can still approve money or documents for a retired club. The club can't withdraw them, because PHASE_CAPABILITIES.RETIRED = [] (authz/index.ts:69). reinstateClub doesn't reopen the tasks. I'm rating this medium, not high, because the funding desk (adminFundingQueue / adminFundingOverview, funding.ts:777-835) still lists SUBMITTED requests and OPEN invoices by record status, so they don't disappear entirely. They do drop out of /tasks and out of the task-based 'Waiting on WSUSA' counts (analytics/admin.ts:33-49), and those numbers then disagree with the funding desk.
google.fix: Inside the retireClub transaction, before the task update: (1) `tx.fundingRequest.updateMany({ where: { clubId: club.id, status: "SUBMITTED" }, data: { status: "WITHDRAWN", decidedAt: now, decisionNote: "Club retired" } })`; (2) `tx.clubDocument.updateMany({ where: { clubId: club.id, status: "PENDING_APPROVAL" }, data: { status: "SUPERSEDED", decidedAt: now } })`. Then narrow the task cancel to `where: { clubId: club.id, status: "OPEN", NOT: { sourceType: { in: ["invoice", "reviewFlag", "reviewBombing"] } } }`, so money that was already approved keeps its INVOICE reminder and the moderation items stay open.

google.title: Two clubs with the same name can both be approved: the name check runs at create and rename but not at submission or approval
google.evidence: assertNameFree ignores drafts: `status: { in: ["SUBMITTED", "CHANGES_REQUESTED", "APPROVED"] }` (clubs.ts:116-123). It is called only from createClub (clubs.ts:198) and from updateClubProfile on a rename (clubs.ts:294). submitForReview (clubs.ts:461-506) and decideClub (clubs.ts:524-570) never call it, and the Club table has no name index (psql pg_indexes: only Club_pkey, Club_slug_key, Club_status_idx). Two founders can each create a draft named 'Chess Club'. Both are allowed because the other is still a draft, both can be submitted, and both can be approved. The slugs differ, so nothing stops it.
google.fix: In submitForReview, call `await assertNameFree(club.name, club.id)` after the status check (before the foundingChecklist/transaction). In decideClub, when `v.decision === "APPROVE"`, call it again.

google.title: Retiring a College Ambassadors org leaves its placements active in other clubs, and the org can no longer end them
google.evidence: retireClub ends only the org's own roles: `tx.roleAssignment.updateMany({ where: { clubId: club.id, endedAt: null }, ... })`. Placements are AMBASSADOR assignments in other clubs with `viaClubId: org.id` (roles.ts:409-417), so they stay active. endPlacement requires `assertClubCap(actor, a.viaClubId, "roster")` (roles.ts:446), and capabilities are filtered by PHASE_CAPABILITIES[club.status] even for admins (authz/index.ts:173-174, RETIRED = []), so nobody on the org side can end them. Only each host club's own leaders can.
google.fix: In the retireClub transaction, add `await tx.roleAssignment.updateMany({ where: { viaClubId: club.id, endedAt: null }, data: { endedAt: now, endReason: "CLUB_RETIRED" } })`. reinstateClub's role query (`clubId: club.id, endReason: "CLUB_RETIRED", endedAt: retiredAt`) should then also match `viaClubId: club.id` so the placements come back.

google.title: Several state transitions check status before writing without a guarded update, so double submits or concurrent admins create duplicate decisions, tasks or roles
google.evidence: submitForReview checks status at clubs.ts:465 and then writes unconditionally with `tx.club.update({ where: { id: club.id }, data: { status: "SUBMITTED", ... } })` (clubs.ts:472). createTask has no dedupe (tasks.ts:47-63), so two concurrent calls write two SUBMITTED ClubDecisions and two admin APPROVAL tasks. decideClub has the same shape (check at clubs.ts:529, update at 549), so two admins can overwrite each other. decideMembership checks `m.status !== "PENDING"` and then calls update (memberships.ts:61-65), and the member can get both the approved and the declined notification. acceptAdvisorInvite counts existing ADVISOR roles (advisors.ts:162-163) before grantRole, so a double accept can create two. RoleAssignment has no unique index (psql pg_indexes: pkey plus two non-unique indexes), so assignRole's holder and capacity check (roles.ts:147-152) can be raced past maxHolders. Funding already uses the safe pattern: `updateMany({ where: { id, status: "SUBMITTED" } })` and throw when count is 0 (funding.ts:636-641).
google.fix: Use the funding claim pattern inside each transaction: submitForReview `tx.club.updateMany({ where: { id: club.id, status: { in: ["DRAFT", "CHANGES_REQUESTED"] } }, ... })`, decideClub `where: { id, status: "SUBMITTED" }`, decideMembership `where: { id, status: "PENDING" }`, and accept/decline claim the invite with `where: { id, status: "PENDING" }` before grantRole. Each throws conflict() when count === 0. For seats, add a partial unique index on RoleAssignment(positionId, userId) WHERE endedAt IS NULL, or lock the Position row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) inside grantRole's transaction before counting holders.

google.title: Any club leader, including a DRAFT-club founder, chooses the Workspace account the service account impersonates through domain-wide delegation (Club.contactEmail)
google.evidence: setClubContactEmail checks only `assertClubCap(actor, v.clubId, "profile")`, and createClub accepts contactEmail from any founder (clubs.ts:180, 219). Both validate with optionalEmail (clubs.ts:51-58), which is a syntax check only: no domain check, no ownership check, no admin approval. lib/authz/index.ts:64 grants DRAFT clubs `["profile","orgchart","constitution","files"]`, so any student who starts a club holds these. The address becomes the DWD subject: google-drive.ts schedule() runs `client(club.contactEmail)`. liveClub/driveReady (lines 68-81) check only that contactEmail is set, not club status. rootFolder() then creates a folder in that account's Drive and calls shareRootWithLeaders, which grants the club's leaders `role: "writer"` (lines 418-431). google-calendar.ts:139 `const subject = e.club?.contactEmail ?? PLATFORM_SENDER` with the full calendar scope, and calendarIdFor inserts a calendar into that account. googleCalendarReady also skips any club-status check. Chat (google-chat.ts:28-31) does require APPROVED, but then creates spaces and posts messages as the address. Result: once a sysadmin turns on Drive sync, a student can create a DRAFT club with contactEmail set to another person's @weber.edu address and upload one file. The platform then acts as that person in Google, creating a Drive folder in their account and sharing it back to the student as writer.
google.fix: Treat contactEmail as untrusted until an admin approves it. Add e.g. Club.googleAccountVerifiedAt, set only by an admin action, or restrict it to a sysadmin-configured pattern of IT-provisioned club mailboxes. Make driveReady/liveClub, googleCalendarReady/syncEventToGoogle and googleChatReady return not-live unless the address is verified and club.status === "APPROVED". In setClubContactEmail, clear the verification and reset googleCalendarId, googleDriveFolderId and googleChatSpaceId whenever the address changes.

google.title: Email header injection: CR/LF in user or club names reaches the raw Gmail Subject header
google.evidence:
The raw message is built as `[`From: ...`, `To: ${input.to}`, `Subject: ${input.subject}`, "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8", "", text].join("
")`, with no sanitizing. notify() passes `subject: input.title` (notify.ts:38) and emails by default. Titles interpolate user-controlled names: files.ts:776 `${actor!.name} shared “${item.name}” with you`, tasks.ts:337 `${actor.name} assigned you a task in ${club.name}`, and advisors.ts:63 `Will you advise ${club.name}?`. Profile names are validated only by `z.string().trim().min(2).max(80)` (profiles.ts:93), and club names by NameInput (clubs.ts:162, trim/min/max). `.trim()` removes only leading and trailing whitespace, so internal 
 survive a crafted server-action POST. File names are safe because cleanName strips control characters, but people and club names are not. With the email integration on, a name such as `X
Bcc: victims@…

<phishing text>` adds recipients and replaces the body of mail sent as the platform sender.
google.fix: In sendEmail, reject or strip /[\r\n\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/ in `to` and `subject` before building the message, and RFC 2047-encode non-ASCII subjects (`=?UTF-8?B?...?=`). Also normalize single-line inputs at the source: add `.transform(s => s.replace(/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]+/g, " "))` to ProfileInput.name and clubs NameInput.

google.title: Expo push errors are logged as SENT and dead tokens are never removed
google.evidence: `status: res.ok ? "SENT" : "FAILED"` (push.ts:25) only looks at the HTTP status. Expo's /--/api/v2/push/send returns HTTP 200 when it rejects a message too, with the error in the ticket: `{ data: { status: "error", details: { error: "DeviceNotRegistered" } } }`. Nothing ever deletes a PushToken except removePushToken (devices.ts:39), which is only reached from the app's own sign-out or switch-off. An uninstalled or rotated token therefore stays registered, every later push goes to it again, and the outbox shows those pushes as SENT.
google.fix: In sendPush, when `res.ok`, parse `const t = (await res.json()).data`. Record status FAILED with `error: t.message` when `t.status === 'error'`, and run `db.pushToken.deleteMany({ where: { token } })` when `t.details?.error === 'DeviceNotRegistered'`.

security.title: Google sign-in checks only the email suffix and never the `hd` (hosted domain) claim
security.evidence: verifyIdToken (google.ts:39-48) checks `if (!p?.email || !p.email_verified) throw ...; if (!emailKind(p.email)) throw ...` and never reads `p.hd`. googleAuthUrl sends `hd: "*"`, which is only a hint, and its comment says "the callback enforces both domains", which it does not. exchangeCode (web callback) and the mobile ID-token route both go through verifyIdToken. emailKind (institution.ts:32-37) maps the suffix to STUDENT or FACULTY_STAFF. A consumer Google account registered with an @weber.edu address passes, for example one a former employee created before leaving, which keeps email_verified=true. That account gets a FACULTY_STAFF user, which can be invited to advise a club. Google treats a non-Gmail address as authoritative only when `hd` is present.
security.fix: In verifyIdToken, after the email_verified check, require `p.hd` and check that it is one of the institution's Workspace domains, e.g. `if (!p.hd || ![INSTITUTION.staffEmailDomain, INSTITUTION.studentEmailDomain].includes(p.hd.toLowerCase())) throw new Error("Sign in with your Weber State Google account.")`. If mail.weber.edu turns out to be a secondary domain of the same tenant, make the allowed hd list configurable. Keep using emailKind for the account kind.

security.title: Open redirect after Google sign-in: the `next` check accepts `/\host` and `/<tab>/host`
security.evidence: app/api/auth/google/route.ts:9-11 stores the raw `next` query parameter in the wc_oauth cookie. After a real login, the callback does `if (next.startsWith("/") && !next.startsWith("//")) dest = next;` and then `redirect(dest)` (callback/route.ts:21, 25). Next 16.4.2 copies the redirect URL into the response unchanged: redirect.js:44 stores it in the digest, and app-route/module.js:237-243 builds `new Headers({ Location: url })`. With `?next=/%5Cevil.example` or `?next=/%09/evil.example`, the Location header is `/\evil.example` or `/\t/evil.example`. Browsers treat backslash as a slash and strip tabs, so both resolve to //evil.example and send the user off-site right after a genuine WSU login. app/login/actions.ts:10-12 safeNext has the same check, but only for test personas, which are off in production.
security.fix: Add one shared helper, e.g. in lib/auth: `export function safeNext(n?: string | null) { if (!n || !/^\/[^\/\\\s]/.test(n) && n !== "/") return "/dashboard"; const u = new URL(n, "http://x"); return u.origin === "http://x" ? u.pathname + u.search + u.hash : "/dashboard"; }`. Apply it in app/api/auth/google/route.ts before writing the cookie, again in callback/route.ts:21, and in place of the local safeNext in app/login/actions.ts.

security.title: Stored XSS: an uploaded XML file (or any unknown-extension file with a client-chosen XML type) is served inline on the app origin
security.evidence: uploadFile (lib/domain/files.ts:1045) stores `mimeType: guessMime(name, input.mimeType)`, and guessMime returns `MIME_BY_EXT[ext] ?? fallback` (lib/files/storage.ts:45-47). MIME_BY_EXT has no xml entry, so the type the client sent is stored for x.xml, or for any unknown extension. scope=user is always allowed (`ownerId = actor.id; allowed = true`, files.ts ~1018), and canViewFile returns true for PUBLIC files even when the viewer is signed out (files.ts:107). The serve route defuses only `type.includes("html")` (line 47, so xhtml is covered), and it adds the sandbox CSP only for `type.includes("svg")` (line 56). text/xml and application/xml are therefore sent as-is with `content-disposition: inline`. An XML document whose root is in the XHTML namespace runs its <script> on the app origin. The app sends no CSP: `curl -sI /clubs` shows no CSP header, next.config.ts has no headers(), and the only CSP in src is this SVG one. The session cookie is SameSite=Lax, so it is sent when the victim follows a link to /api/files/<id>. The script can then call server actions as the victim, including admin actions when the victim is an admin.
security.fix: In /api/files/[id]/route.ts, serve inline only an allowlist (application/pdf, image/png|jpeg|gif|webp, video/mp4|quicktime, audio/mpeg, text/plain). Send every other type with `content-disposition: attachment` and `content-type: application/octet-stream`, and add `content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` to every response, not just SVG. In storage.ts guessMime, stop trusting the client type for unknown extensions: return `MIME_BY_EXT[ext] ?? "application/octet-stream"`.

security.title: .env.example sets AUTH_MODE="both", which overrides the production-safe default and enables passwordless sign-in as any account
security.evidence: authMode() (lib/auth/google.ts:51-55) defaults to "google" when NODE_ENV is production, but only if AUTH_MODE is unset. .env.example line 6 sets `AUTH_MODE="both"`, and README.md:23 tells operators to `cp .env.example .env` (README:52 also points to .env.example for the Google credentials). Any deployment built from the template therefore has personas on. The local production build shows the effect: `curl localhost:3200/api/m/auth/personas` returns `"personasEnabled":true`, and /login renders "Test personas" and "Sign in as any university email". Note that :3200 is a local smoke test using the dev .env; the real exposure comes from deploying with the template. In that mode signInWithTestEmail (login/actions.ts:25-31) calls `findOrCreateUserByEmail({ email, ... }); await signInWeb(user.id)` with no secret, so anyone can sign in as an existing admin or advisor. Persona sign-in also lists the SYSADMIN persona.
security.fix: Delete the AUTH_MODE line from .env.example, or set it to "google" with a comment that "both"/"mock" are for local development only. In authMode(), when NODE_ENV === "production", return "google" unless an explicit ALLOW_TEST_SIGNIN=1 is also set. The web actions and /api/m/auth/persona already go through personasEnabled(), so this one change guards them all.

security.title: Open redirect through `next` (login page for signed-in users; OAuth start/callback via a backslash)
security.evidence: login/page.tsx:16 `const next = sp.next && sp.next.startsWith("/") ? sp.next : "/dashboard"`, then line 18 `if (user && !sp.switch) redirect(next)`. Next 16 puts the URL into Location verbatim (app-render.js:2501 `addPathPrefix(getURLFromRedirectError(err), basePath)`, and addPathPrefix is a no-op with no basePath), so a signed-in user who opens /login?next=//evil.example lands off-site. /api/auth/google/route.ts:9 stores `next` unvalidated in the wc_oauth cookie. The callback (callback/route.ts:21) and login/actions.ts:11 reject only a leading `//`, so `next=/\evil.example` passes, and browsers read `/\` as `//`. The page's Google button forwards next (page.tsx:42), so the user is sent off-site right after a real Weber State sign-in.
security.fix: Add one shared safeNext(next) in lib/auth, and use it in login/page.tsx, login/actions.ts, api/auth/google/route.ts (before writing the cookie) and the callback. It should return next only if it starts with "/", does not start with "//" or "/\\", and contains no "\\". Alternatively: `const u = new URL(next, appOrigin); return u.origin === appOrigin ? u.pathname + u.search + u.hash : "/dashboard"`.

security.title: Upload routes buffer the whole request body before the auth and size checks (unauthenticated memory exhaustion)
security.evidence: upload/route.ts:15-16 runs `const actor = await getCurrentUser(); const form = await req.formData()...`, and line 28 runs `Buffer.from(await file.arrayBuffer())`. assertSignedIn and the `input.bytes.length > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` check happen only later, inside uploadFile (files.ts ~999-1002). api/constitution/documents/route.ts:14-17 has the same order. proxy.ts's matcher excludes `api/`, and next.config.ts sets no body limit, so a signed-out client can POST arbitrarily large multipart bodies that are held fully in memory before anything rejects them.
security.fix: In both routes, return 401 when `actor` is null before calling req.formData(). Return 413 when `content-length` is missing or greater than MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES plus about 64 KB of multipart overhead. Better still, parse with a streaming multipart parser (e.g. busboy with limits.fileSize = MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES).

security.title: Private calendar-feed token (and advisor invite token) defaults to Prisma cuid(), leaving only about 41 random bits
security.evidence: `calendarToken String @unique @default(cuid())` is the only secret on /api/ics/user/<token> (route.ts:14 looks the user up by it), a feed that includes the user's members-only events. In the live DB the tokens share structure: `cmvbrxria0000rxv6qhnv6zph`, `cmvbrxrih0082rxv633gmcpdr`, `cmvbrxrii0094rxv6fpai2te1`. Timestamp, sequential counter and host fingerprint are predictable, and only the last 8 base36 characters (about 41 bits) are random, below the usual 64+ bits for a long-lived bearer token. resetCalendarToken (memberships.ts:156) already uses randomUUID, but every account starts with the cuid value. AdvisorInvite.token (schema.prisma:484) uses the same default.
security.fix: Remove `@default(cuid())` from calendarToken and AdvisorInvite.token. Set them in code with `randomBytes(32).toString("base64url")` in findOrCreateUserByEmail/user creation and in the invite creation in advisors.ts. Add a one-time migration that rotates existing calendarToken values.

security.title: Capability-holder routing for tasks and notifications ignores the requirement suspension that getClubAccess applies
security.evidence: clubCapabilityHolders (people.ts:16), clubsWhereUserHolds (:42) and tasks.taskScopeFor (tasks.ts:82) use `r.role === "ADVISOR" || r.role === "PRESIDENT" || r.role === "VP" || r.permissions.includes(cap)`. getClubAccess clears every capability when `suspended = status.overdue` (authz/index.ts:163-172). DB: Jose Cox, Pride Alliance OFFICER with {events,attendance}, last passed the officer test in cycle 2024-2025 and has no training check-in, so he is past the 30-day grace and suspended. He would still receive notifyClubCapability notices (notify.ts:49-50) and CLUB tasks for 'events' and 'attendance', which open to the NoPermission page. Rated low: advisors are always holders and never suspended, so tasks still reach someone who can act. Club phase has no effect today because no tasks exist for capabilities outside the phase.
security.fix: In lib/authz/people.ts, add a single holdsCapability check that also drops student leaders of APPROVED clubs whose requirementStatus(...).overdue is true. Use it in clubCapabilityHolders and clubsWhereUserHolds, and have taskScopeFor call clubsWhereUserHolds (or the shared predicate) instead of its own copy.

security.title: Open redirect: /login sends signed-in users to any next= URL, and the shared guards miss "/\"
security.evidence: `const next = sp.next && sp.next.startsWith("/") ? sp.next : "/dashboard"; ... if (user && !sp.switch) redirect(next);` means /login?next=//evil.example sends a signed-in visitor to evil.example (proxy.ts makes no auth or URL decisions). safeNext in login/actions.ts:10-12 and the Google callback (api/auth/google/callback/route.ts:21) block "//" but not "/\evil.example", which browsers resolve as //evil.example. lib/rich/embeds.ts:58 (safeLinkTarget) already rejects `/\`, so the codebase knows about this case.
security.fix: Add one exported `safeNext(next)` in lib/auth that accepts only `/^\/(?![\/\\])/` and no control characters, falling back to "/dashboard". Use it in login/page.tsx:16, login/actions.ts:10, api/auth/google/route.ts:9 (before saving the cookie) and api/auth/google/callback/route.ts:21.

security.title: Login page shows any ?error= text, and the Google callback puts raw exception messages there
security.evidence: `redirect(`/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Sign-in failed")}`)`, and login/page.tsx:35-38 renders `{sp.error}` in a danger Callout. GET :3200/login?error=Your%20account%20is%20locked.%20Call%20801-555-0100 renders that sentence as an official error. React escapes it, so this is text injection, not XSS, and it lets internal Prisma or token-exchange messages reach the page: low.
security.fix: Redirect with codes (?error=expired|cancelled|domain|failed), including the two hard-coded redirects at lines 13 and 15. Map the codes to fixed copy in login/page.tsx and ignore unknown values. Log the real exception with console.error on the server only. In api/m/auth/google/route.ts:33, return a fixed message rather than e.message from findOrCreateUserByEmail.

events.title: .ics download and the assistant's event_details refuse members of an approved co-host club access to members-only events

Its cohosts are `cohosts: { where: { status: "APPROVED" }, select: { club: { select: { id, name, slug } } } }` (lib/events/feed.ts:112), so each item is `{ club }` with no clubId or status. Domain canViewEvent (lib/domain/events.ts:167) passes the whole object on to eventAccess. eventAccess (lib/authz/events.ts:85-90) uses `event.cohosts` whenever it is present and runs `if (c.status !== "APPROVED") continue;`. Every co-host is skipped, so a co-host member gets `{ok:false, reason:"members"}` and a 404. lib/ai/read-tools.ts:567 selects `cohosts: {..., select: { club: { select: { name: true } } } }` and fails the same way at line 572. The event page (app/events/[id]/page.tsx:36 uses `include`, so it has the full EventCohost rows) shows these members the event and its 'Add to calendar' link (page.tsx:176 → /api/ics/occurrence/<id>), and that link then returns 404. In lib/ai/read-tools.ts:567 select `cohosts: { where: { status: "APPROVED" }, select: { clubId: true, status: true, club: { select: { name: true } } } }`. Change the parameter type of domain canViewEvent (lib/domain/events.ts:167) to `EventGate` from @/lib/authz/events. events.title: All-day event end handling is wrong: every all-day date range shows two days, and on DST days the occurrence spans two days in the calendar and ICS or fails to mirror to Google
events.evidence: `const durMs = (spec.allDay ? 24 * 60 : ...) * 60_000;` sets endsAt = start + 24 h (push at line 70, the NONE branch at 76, the no-term fallback at 128). Running it with tsx for all-day Sun Mar 14 2027 gives 2027-03-14T07:00Z→2027-03-15T07:00Z, which is 01:00 MDT on Mar 15. feed.ts:180 `addDaysToDateInput(toDateInput(endsAt-1ms),1)` then gives the end '2027-03-16', and ics.ts:108-109 writes DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20270316, so the event covers two days. For Sun Nov 1 2026 the run gives 06:00Z→2026-11-02T06:00Z (23:00 MST Nov 1). google-calendar.ts:97 `{ date: toDateInput(new Date(first.startsAt.getTime() + 86_400_000)) }` = '2026-11-01', the same as the start date, so Google gets an empty all-day range and the sync fails. Separately, lib/time.ts:31 fmtRange compares start with the exclusive end, so every all-day event renders as two dates. A tsx run of `fmtRange(campusDate(2026,10,20), +24h, true)` returns 'Oct 20 – Oct 21'. That string appears on the event page, the calendar popover, cards, the mobile API whenLabel and the assistant. The DB has no all-day events yet (count 0), but the editor and drag-and-drop both create them.
events.fix: In recurrence.ts add `const endOf = (s: Date) => { if (!spec.allDay) return new Date(s.getTime() + durMs); const n = shiftDays(local(s), 1); return campusDate(n.y, n.m, n.d, 0, 0); };` and use `endsAt: endOf(...)` at the three push sites (lines 70, 76, 128). In google-calendar.ts:97 use `{ date: addDaysToDateInput(toDateInput(first.startsAt), 1) }` (import from @/lib/events/wallclock). In lib/time.ts:30 use `const e = inCampusTime(allDay ? new Date(new Date(end).getTime() - 1) : end);`.

events.title: Any save of the Club Officer Training event deletes its upcoming Oct 28 makeup session
events.evidence: writeEvent always runs `await materialize(tx, event.id, desired, ...)`. materialize (line 381) deletes every future occurrence that has no check-ins and that the rule does not produce. The seed (prisma/seed/steps/events.ts:282-300) adds makeup sessions as extra occurrences of the training event. They have to live on that event, because RoleRequirement fulfillment counts only check-ins at `trainingEventId` (lib/authz/requirements.ts:51-55). A tsx run of expandOccurrences with the real Term rows for the stored rule (SEMESTERLY from 2024-09-10T23:30Z, until 2027-05-01T05:00Z) gives 6 dates. Stored are 8: the past, attended makeup on 2026-10-07 stays locked, but the future makeup 2026-10-28T23:30Z (note 'Makeup session for officers who started mid-semester', 0 check-ins) is not produced by the rule and would be deleted. Gating on `scheduleChanged` is not enough. The editor turns the stored until (2027-04-30 23:00 campus time) into `fromInputs(date, "23:59")` = 05:59Z (components/events/when.ts:78,98), so sameSchedule is false on any save from /admin/trainings/<id>. Correction to the original evidence: 7 open 'Attend: Club Officer Training' tasks link to this event, not 20.
events.fix: In writeEvent, rebuild occurrences only when the meeting times actually change. Before the transaction: `const prior = existing && existing.status !== "DRAFT" && existing.startsAt ? expandOccurrences({ startsAt: existing.startsAt, durationMinutes: existing.durationMinutes, allDay: existing.allDay, recurrence: existing.recurrence, interval: existing.recurrenceInterval, weekdays: existing.recurrenceWeekdays, until: existing.recurrenceUntil, count: existing.recurrenceCount }, terms) : null; const timesChanged = !prior || prior.length !== desired.length || prior.some((o, i) => o.startsAt.getTime() !== desired[i].startsAt.getTime() || o.endsAt.getTime() !== desired[i].endsAt.getTime());`. Then call materialize only `if (timesChanged)` (line 623).

events.title: Cancelling a past meeting that has check-ins removes that attendance from every metric and the tracker
events.evidence: cancelOccurrence (lines 833-840) checks only `if (occ.status === "CANCELLED") return` and then sets status CANCELLED, with no check for check-ins. EventsBuilder.tsx:399 `{manage && !p.cancelled ? (` offers 'Cancel this meeting' on any meeting the calendar shows, past ones included. Metrics and tracker queries keep only `o.status = 'SCHEDULED'` (lib/metrics/index.ts:130,135; lib/attendance/queries.ts:124-127 clubOccurrencesWhere). Once the meeting is cancelled, its check-ins drop out of held events, active status, review eligibility, retention and the tracker. The Attendance rows remain. This goes against the module's own rule that 'meetings with check-ins are kept as history' (events.ts:29-33) and the contract's rule that attended past meetings of cancelled events still count (contracts.md:29). cancelEvent itself touches only `startsAt >= now`.
events.fix: In cancelOccurrence, after the CANCELLED early return, add `if (await db.attendance.count({ where: { occurrenceId: occ.id } })) throw conflict("People already checked in to this meeting, so it can't be cancelled. Remove their check-ins first if it didn't happen.");`. Leave the metrics filters unchanged.

events.title: Moving a one-time event that has check-ins moves its attendance history to the new date
events.evidence: In materialize's one-time branch (`} else if (existing.length === 1 && desired.length === 1) {`, lines 354-358), the occurrence is updated whenever its times differ. Unlike the repeating branch (line 360 `locked = existing.filter((o) => o.startsAt < now || o._count.attendances > 0)`), it never checks `o._count.attendances`. That breaks the module's own rule (lines 29-31: 'past meetings and meetings with check-ins are kept as history'). lib/events/feed.ts:191 `editable: canManage && hostedHere && e.recurrence === "NONE" && !cancelled` makes past one-time events draggable, and moveEvent and updateEvent have no guard. Dragging an attended meeting to next week turns its check-ins into check-ins at a future meeting. It stops counting as held, its month and term buckets change, and checkedInAt now falls before startsAt.
events.fix: In the one-time branch: `const moved = o.startsAt.getTime() !== d.startsAt.getTime() || o.endsAt.getTime() !== d.endsAt.getTime(); if (moved && o.startsAt.getTime() !== d.startsAt.getTime() && o._count.attendances > 0) throw conflict("People already checked in to this event, so its date can't change. Create a new event instead."); if (moved) toUpdate.push({ id: o.id, ...d });`. This still allows changing only the end time. In feed.ts:191 add `&& o.endsAt > new Date()` so past events aren't offered for drag.

events.title: ICS escapeText never escapes semicolons, and the unit test asserts the same no-op
events.evidence: `.replace(/;/g, "\;")`: in a JS string `"\;"` is just `";"`, so the replace changes nothing. ics.test.ts:9 expects `"a\\\\b\;c\\,d\\ne"`, which has the same unescaped `;`, so the test passes. The live /api/ics/university feed has DESCRIPTION lines with a bare `;` ('Wear comfortable clothes; we'll provide water and snacks.'), and RFC 5545 §3.3.11 requires `\;`. Severity lowered from medium because mainstream clients tolerate a bare `;` in TEXT values. It is still a clear code bug.
events.fix: ics.ts:46 → `.replace(/;/g, "\\;")`. ics.test.ts:9 → `.toBe("a\\\\b\\;c\\,d\\ne")`, so the test actually checks for the backslash.

events.title: Restoring a cancelled event also un-cancels its earlier one-off (holiday) cancellations and wipes their notes
events.evidence: restoreEvent: `tx.eventOccurrence.updateMany({ where: { eventId, status: "CANCELLED", startsAt: { gte: new Date() } }, data: { status: "SCHEDULED", note: null } })`. This brings back every upcoming cancelled meeting, including ones cancelled on their own before the event-level cancel. The DB has 11 future one-off cancellations on SCHEDULED events, all with the note 'No meeting — Thanksgiving break' (e.g. Lab Night and General Meeting, Nov 25-27). After a cancel then restore of one of those events, the Thanksgiving meeting is back on calendars and feeds and its note is gone. contracts.md:149 states this behavior, but it contradicts the module's rule that one-off cancellations survive schedule changes.
events.fix: In cancelEvent, before the updateMany, read the ids of upcoming occurrences that are already CANCELLED: `const kept = (await tx.eventOccurrence.findMany({ where: { eventId, status: "CANCELLED", startsAt: { gte: now } }, select: { id: true } })).map((o) => o.id)`. Store them in the event.cancelled log data (`keptCancelledIds: kept`). In restoreEvent, load the latest `event.cancelled` ActivityLog for the event and add `id: { notIn: keptCancelledIds }` to the updateMany. Update contracts.md:149 to match.

events.title: Every-semester or every-academic-year rule starting between terms puts every meeting in a break
events.evidence: When no term contains the start, `home` is the next term, and `offset = daysBetween(local(home.startsOn), start)` (line 130) is negative. Every later term gets that offset. The only guard, `> t.endsOn` (line 138), never catches dates before t.startsOn. A tsx run with the real Term rows for SEMESTERLY from 2026-12-29T01:00Z (Mon Dec 28 at 6 PM campus time), count 4, gives Dec 28 2026, Aug 16 2027 and Dec 27 2027. All three fall between terms: Spring 2027 starts Jan 11, Fall 2027 starts Aug 30. Count 4 also yields only 3 meetings. The editor preview does show these dates, which limits the impact.
events.fix: In the SEMESTERLY/ACADEMIC_YEARLY case use `const offset = Math.max(0, daysBetween(local(home.startsOn), start));`, so a start between terms lands on the first day of each term. Also add `if (campusDate(p.y, p.m, p.d) < t.startsOn) continue;` next to the endsOn guard.

events.title: ICS feeds with no events emit a VCALENDAR with zero components

events.title: Same-day events that cross noon print the start time with no AM or PM ("10:00 – 2:00 PM")
