mobile.title: Tapping "Sign in to register" on mobile only signs you in; it never registers you
mobile.evidence: The signed-out button only runs `router.push({ pathname: '/welcome', params: { reason: 'register' } })` (club/[slug].tsx:235-238). Nothing records that the person wanted to join: grepping apps/mobile/src for 'register' finds only welcome.tsx:89-90 (the notice text) and this push. welcome.tsx `finish` calls `await signIn(await start()); close();` and does nothing else (welcome.tsx:42-56). After sign-in the useApi key changes to `club:${user.id}:slug` (line 34), so the page reloads and shows the plain Register button (line 278), and the person has to tap it again. The web carries the intent through login: `loginHref(slug, register)` adds `?register=1` (MembershipControls.tsx:25-27), and the effect at lines 78-95 calls `register(stripParam)` once signed in. The spec (docs/spec.md:20-21) describes the flow as clicking register, logging in, and then being registered.
mobile.fix: In ClubScreen, add `const wantsJoin = useRef(false)` and set `wantsJoin.current = true` in the signed-out button's onPress before the push. Pass a callback prop into Actions for this. Add a `useFocusEffect` above the early returns. When `wantsJoin.current` is set and `data?.viewer.signedIn` is true, clear the ref and call `Api.clubAction(slug, 'join')` once (or move `act` above the early returns and call `act('join')`), but only if `!data.viewer.isMember && !data.viewer.isPending`. If the person is still signed out (they chose "Not now"), just clear the ref.

mobile.title: After an offline sign-out the phone keeps getting that account's push notifications, and a failed 'notifications off' is never retried
mobile.evidence: signOut: `try { await Api.signOut(current, pushToken); } catch { /* Offline ... */ } await removeItem(KEYS.pushToken); ... await forget();` (session.tsx:147-160). The server is the only place that deletes the PushToken row (auth/signout/route.ts:18-21 → devices.ts:39 `deleteMany({ where: { token, userId } })`). If that request never arrives, the row stays linked to the user, and the phone has already deleted the token and the session it would need to retry. sendPush sends to every row with `db.pushToken.findMany({ where: { userId } })` (lib/integrations/push.ts:10), without checking any session, and PushToken has no session link (schema.prisma:220-227). The phone shows 'signed out' but keeps showing that account's notification titles and bodies until someone else signs in and registerPushToken moves the token. The same gap exists for setPushEnabled(false): if removal fails, the catch says 'Try again next launch' (lines 175-177), but syncPush returns as soon as it sees 'off' (lines 81-84), so the removal is never retried.
mobile.fix: Add a storage key, e.g. `KEYS.pendingSignOut`. In signOut's catch, save `{ token: current, pushToken }` under it. The revoke never reached the server, so that session token is still valid there. In the launch effect and the AppState 'active' handler, if the key exists, call `Api.signOut(saved.token, saved.pushToken)` and delete the key when it succeeds. In syncPush, before the `=== 'off'` early return, if `KEYS.pushToken` is still stored and `token.current` is set, retry `Api.removePush(stored)` and remove the key when it succeeds. Server-side hardening (optional): add `sessionId` to PushToken with onDelete: Cascade, set from the bearer session in registerPushToken, so revoking or expiring a session also stops its pushes.

mobile.title: On Android, expo-router also routes the Google sign-in redirect and opens the "not found" screen
mobile.evidence: `Google.useIdTokenAuthRequest` defaults the redirect to `${Application.applicationId}:/oauthredirect` (node_modules/expo-auth-session/build/providers/Google.js:146-148). On Android, expo-web-browser waits for that redirect through `Linking.addEventListener('url', ...)` (expo-web-browser/build/WebBrowser.js:304-350, the polyfill used on Android). expo-router subscribes to the same 'url' events (expo-router/build/link/linking.js:165-178) with `prefixes: []` (getLinkingConfig.js:72). Every URL becomes a path through fromDeepLink (fork/extractPathFromURL.js:83-116), and useLinking.native.js:109-128 enqueues NAVIGATE_TO_HREF for it. The app has no `src/app/+native-intent.tsx` and no `oauthredirect` route (ls src/app: (tabs), +not-found.tsx, _layout.tsx, c, club, event, welcome.tsx), so `/oauthredirect?code=…` opens +not-found on top of the sign-in modal. Then finish() → close() → router.back() (welcome.tsx:24-27, 48) removes only the not-found screen, which leaves the person on the sign-in screen, already signed in. iOS is not affected because ASWebAuthenticationSession returns the URL directly.
mobile.fix: Add `apps/mobile/src/app/+native-intent.tsx`: `export function redirectSystemPath({ path, initial }: { path: string; initial: boolean }) { if (path.includes('oauthredirect')) return initial ? '/' : null; return path; }`. getLinkingConfig.js:65-66 picks this file up automatically, and linking.js:167-174 skips the listener when the function returns a falsy value. expo-auth-session still receives the URL through its own listener.

mobile.title: Calendar weeks added with 'Show 6 more weeks' disappear on the next quiet refetch or pull-to-refresh
mobile.evidence: The fetcher is always `() => Api.calendar()`, which loads the server's default 42 days (views.ts:162, 175). loadMore adds the extra weeks only through `setData` (calendar.tsx:49-58). useApi refetches quietly on focus when the data is older than 30 s or the epoch changed (use-api.ts:79-83, and invalidateApi() runs after every check-in or join). It then replaces the data with `setState({ data, ... })` (use-api.ts:53-56). Switching tabs and coming back drops the loaded weeks and resets 'Showing through …'.
mobile.fix: In Agenda, add `const [to, setTo] = useState<string | undefined>()` and change the fetcher to `() => Api.calendar(undefined, to)`. Keep the key unchanged. useApi refreshes fetcherRef on every render, and the server accepts `to` without `from` (views.ts:174-175). In loadMore, call `setTo(next.to)` after merging.

mobile.title: The Android push setup leaves out FCM, so following the README gives Android builds no push token
mobile.evidence: The `android` block (app.json:20-29) has no `googleServicesFile`. No eas.json exists, and nothing in apps/mobile/README.md, app.json or docs mentions FCM, Firebase or google-services.json (grep finds none). The README push section (README.md:123-126) says an EAS project id is all a push token needs. On Android development and store builds, `Notifications.getExpoPushTokenAsync` needs Firebase set up (google-services.json, plus FCM V1 credentials in EAS for delivery). Without it the call throws, lib/push.ts:63-64 catches it as 'unavailable', and Android users never get pushes.
mobile.fix: Add `"googleServicesFile": "./google-services.json"` to `expo.android` in app.json, with the file provided as an EAS file secret rather than committed. Extend README.md's 'Push notifications' section with an Android step: create a Firebase project for `android.package`, download google-services.json, and upload the FCM V1 service-account key with `eas credentials`.

mobile.title: In the mobile app, notifications for web-only pages open a signed-out in-app browser
mobile.evidence: openHref falls back to `openWeb(href)` (WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync on `${API_URL}${path}`) for anything routeForHref doesn't map. The app authenticates with a bearer token, and api/m/auth has only google, persona, personas and signout (no web-session handoff). Notification hrefs in the DB include /tasks (15), /admin (12), /tests (5), /messages (3) and /clubs/<x>/manage/* (several), all of which need a web sign-in. The first tap lands on /login, contrary to the comment at lines 8-11. After one web sign-in the in-app browser keeps the cookie, so this is friction rather than a dead end: low.
mobile.fix: Add POST /api/m/auth/web-link, which issues a short-lived single-use token, and a GET route that exchanges it for a web session cookie and redirects to a safeNext()-checked path. Have openWeb call it for same-origin paths. Failing that, label these rows "Opens on the web, sign-in required".

ux.title: Mobile nav panel stays open after navigating by any link outside it, and Escape doesn't close it
ux.evidence: `open` is reset only by the toggle and by onClick on the panel's own links. There is no effect on `path`, no keydown handler and no backdrop, and the header persists across navigations in the root layout. Reproduced at 375px: opened the menu, clicked the header logo, and after navigation the toggle still had aria-expanded="true" and the fixed panel was still rendered. A dispatched Escape keydown left it open.
ux.fix: In MobileNav add `useEffect(() => setOpen(false), [path]);`, plus a document keydown listener while open that closes on Escape and returns focus to the toggle. Optionally add a transparent backdrop that closes on click.

ux.title: Star ratings are labelled on a role-less span, so screen readers drop them, and club cards also hide the number
ux.evidence: `<span className="inline-flex …" aria-label={`${value.toFixed(1)} out of 5 stars`}>` has no role. ARIA doesn't allow naming a generic element, so assistive tech generally ignores the label. Per-review ratings (components/reviews/ClubReviews.tsx:212) have no other text. RatingInline (components/clubs/ClubCard.tsx:34-36) marks the numeric average `aria-hidden="true"` and relies on this label, so club-card ratings are lost too.
ux.fix: Add `role="img"` to the Stars wrapper span (keeping aria-label), or render `{value.toFixed(1)} out of 5 stars` inside it and drop the aria-label.

ux.title: Navigation menus don't expose the current page (no aria-current), and locked workspace tools are only dimmed
ux.evidence: WorkspaceNav (line 23 computes `active`), SideNav (components/workspace/SideNav.tsx:13), NavLinks and MobileNav (components/shell/NavLinks.tsx:20-23, 44-48) use the active state only for classes. grep finds aria-current only in page-level tab switches. Locked links in WorkspaceNav are marked only with `l.locked && "opacity-55"` (line 31). manage/layout.tsx sets locked when a capability is missing.
ux.fix: Add `aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined}` to the Link in all four navs. In WorkspaceNav, when `l.locked`, add a Lock icon (aria-hidden) and ` (no access)`.

ux.title: "Log in to add this calendar to yours" doesn't add it after login
ux.evidence: The signed-out switch links to `loginHref(slug)`, i.e. /login?next=/clubs/<slug> with no hand-off flag. Register passes `?register=1` and auto-registers on return (lines 25-27, 79-95). Subscribe has no equivalent, so the user comes back unsubscribed and has to toggle again.
ux.fix: Extend loginHref to take a `subscribe` flag that appends `?subscribe=1`, and pass it at line 157. In the club page or SubscribeToggle, when signedIn and the flag is present and not yet subscribed, call setClubSubscription(clubId, true) once, then strip the parameter with router.replace, as RegisterButton does.

ux.title: Signed-in header at 375px leaves the logo about 119px, so "Wildcat Clubs" wraps onto two lines
ux.evidence: Measured at 375px: the logo link needs 152.5px (the wordmark span is 110.5px) and the row uses gap-4 in a 343px content box. Signed in, the right cluster is 3×36px icon links + 3×4px gaps + ml-1 + a 32px avatar = 156px. 343 − 36 (menu) − 156 − 2×16 (gaps) = 119px for the logo, so the span wraps at the space (its min-content is "Wildcat").
ux.fix: Add `whitespace-nowrap` to the wordmark span in components/shell/Logo.tsx:19 and use `gap-2 sm:gap-4` on the header row. Or hide the wordmark below sm when signed in (`hidden sm:inline`).

ux.title: Footer hard-codes two policy slugs that 404 once either policy is archived
ux.evidence: The footer links `/policies/review-integrity` and `/policies/anonymous-reporting`. Admins can archive published policies (lib/domain/policies.ts:166; deletePolicy's error says "Archive it instead — it leaves the library and the app"). policyBySlug (policies.ts:219) returns null for non-PUBLISHED policies to non-admins, so after an archive, every page's footer links to a 404. Today both are PUBLISHED with placements REVIEWS and COMPLAINTS.
ux.fix: Make SiteFooter an async server component that looks up the published policy with placement REVIEWS and the one with COMPLAINTS, linking each slug if present and omitting the link otherwise.

ux.title: No app/global-error.tsx, so a failure in the root layout's header shows Next's unbranded error page
ux.evidence: The root layout renders <SiteHeader/>, which on every request runs getCurrentUser, db.notification.count, countOpenTasks and countUnreadConversations (SiteHeader.tsx:25-28). app/error.tsx sits below the root layout and can't catch its errors, and `ls src/app/global-error.tsx` shows no such file.
ux.fix: Add apps/web/src/app/global-error.tsx ("use client", with its own <html><body>) using the same copy and reset button as app/error.tsx. Optionally wrap SiteHeader's count queries in a catch that falls back to 0.
